issues.description: The script sends latitude and longitude coordinates to nominatim.openstreetmap.org for reverse geocoding using GM_xmlhttpRequest. This is a third-party service and may receive user location data.
issues.recommendation: Warn users about location data being sent to OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Consider making this optional or informing users.

issues.description: The script requests @connect permission for discord.com, and the description mentions 'send to discord', implying user data (possibly coordinates or game info) can be sent to Discord webhooks.
issues.recommendation: Ensure users are aware of what data is sent to Discord. Do not send sensitive or personal data without explicit user consent.

issues.description: The script uses the Notification API to send browser notifications.
issues.recommendation: Ensure notifications are not abused. Only use with user consent.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission, which is high-privilege and can be abused for data exfiltration.
issues.recommendation: Limit usage to only necessary domains and document all network requests.

issues.description: The script requests Notification API permission, which can be abused for spam.
issues.recommendation: Request permission only when needed and explain to the user.

summary: This script transmits user location data to third-party services (OpenStreetMap Nominatim and potentially Discord), which is a critical privacy and data exfiltration risk. It does not appear to collect other sensitive data or use obfuscation, but the network requests and permissions require user awareness and explicit consent. The script does not appear to have DOM XSS or supply chain risks in the provided code. Overall, the main risk is third-party data transmission.
